title: Quant Autotuner regression causing kernel timeouts and evaluation drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
incident_summary: Canary and production observed intermittent kernel timeouts and increased accuracy drift after enabling the Quant Autotuner. Issues manifested as slow tail latency spikes, occasional model worker restarts, and a 3-6% BLEU/ROUGE degradation on internal evals for a subset of customer models.
root_cause: The Autotuner's fused-kernel selection heuristic started favoring a new attention-fusion path for models that use a mixed-size attention implementation. That fused kernel had an edge-case mismatch in KV cache indexing for odd sequence-length shards, causing intermittent OOB memory reads and timeouts. Simultaneously, the autotuner switched quantization scale calibration to a fast-path estimator for certain activations which underrepresented high-variance tokens, producing measurable eval drift on our canary prompts.
mitigation: Immediate rollback of the autotuner default-profile to the previous stable policy; disable fused-attention kernel selection for model families matching the observed signature; pin converter library to v2.8.3 on affected fleets; temporarily expand canary prompt set and sampling rate to detect regressions sooner.
remediation_timeline: 2026-02-20: Incident detection by canary alert (SRE) -> paged ENG on-call (Aisha).
2026-02-20: Hot rollback of autotuner default-profile to stable (PR #6123 deployed to production fleet).
2026-02-21: Triage meeting: confirmed fused-kernel selection logic and fast-path calibration as suspects.
2026-02-23: Reproduced OOB/timeout in isolated regression harness with seq_len=103 and split-shard config.
2026-02-25: Implemented defensive bounds checks and disabled fusion in runtime (canary rollout).
2026-03-01: Canary showed stability but small remaining eval variance; added extended calibration routine for high-variance activations.
2026-03-05: Merged full fix with unit + harness tests (PR #6189); plan for staged rollout in runtime-1.19.1.
2026-03-10: Post-deployment monitoring OK for 72h; tracking long-tail regression metrics for two weeks.
action_items: ENG-14621: Add unit tests that iterate odd/even shard splits and sequence lengths up to 512 (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 5).
ENG-14622: Extend canary prompt set with edge cases (long-run tokens, high-variance tokens) and increase sample frequency from 0.5% -> 2% of requests (owner: SRE team, estimate: 3).
ENG-14623: Rework Autotuner heuristic to include KV-index-safety check before enabling fused kernels (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 8).
ENG-14624: Add end-to-end quant calibration shadow run in CI for every converter bump, include drift threshold gates (owner: QA, estimate: 5).
ENG-14625: Backfill canary historical eval runs to identify earliest autotuner release that introduced drift (owner: Data Eng, estimate: 3).
ENG-14626: Document fallback policies and emergency runbook for quantization regressions; integrate into incident playbooks (owner: Aisha Kapoor, estimate: 2).
acceptance_criteria: No kernel timeouts or worker restarts attributable to quant fused kernels in 14 days on production telemetry.
Canary eval BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity within 1% of pre-incident baseline for affected model families across 72h of traffic.
Autotuner updates gated by CI shadow-calibration and drift-threshold checks; PR must include regression-harness results.
New unit/regression tests merged and green in mainline; rollout plan documented for runtime-1.19.1.
